back: A sustained improvement in people's economic and social welfare: higher real incomes plus better health, education, services and choice.

front: How does economic development differ from economic growth?
back: Growth is an increase in real output (quantitative); development is a broad improvement in welfare (qualitative). Growth can happen without development.
Higher literacy; lower death rates and longer life expectancy; better infrastructure (water, power, roads); better housing; less poverty.
A UNDP index from 0 to 1 combining life expectancy, years of schooling and GNI per head (at purchasing power parity).

front: Two advantages of real GDP per head as an indicator.
back: Data widely available and comparable; adjusted for inflation and population size.

front: Three disadvantages of real GDP per head.
back: An average that ignores distribution; misses informal and subsistence output; ignores health, education, leisure and pollution.

front: One advantage and two disadvantages of the HDI.
back: Broader than income (includes health and education); but ignores distribution, freedom and the environment, and years of schooling ignore quality.
Economic growth; investment in education and health; infrastructure; good governance; technology and diversification.
